where Zeff(n) is the ­effective nuclear charge in that shell. To understand the origin and magnitude of Zeff(n), consider a particular electron e1 in an atom. Inner elec- trons near the nucleus shield e1 from the full charge Z of the nucleus by effectively canceling some of the positive nuclear charge. Zeff(n) is thus the net reduced nu- clear charge experienced by a particular electron, due to the presence of the other electrons. The effective nuclear charge Zeff(n) is given by (Z2S) where Z is the nu- clear charge and S is the shielding or screening constant for an orbital with princi- pal quantum number n.
